2.
The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:

On 30.09.2023 at about 22.45 hours, when the deceased Rakesh S.G., was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-17- EC-1239 on Doddabele-Rajarajeshwari Road and Lakshmi Devamma M vs Darshan S D on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26956443/

No.KA-01-JV-9678 riding the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased vehicle from back side and caused the accident, due to which, he sustained injuries.

sentences.text: Immediately after the accident, deceased was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru, but inspite of better treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.

Later after conducting post-mortem in the said, the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that, the deceased was studying B.Com., and also working as a Swiggy delivery boy as part-time job and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony, lost love and affection of their son and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-01-JV-9678.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondents appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed written statements.
5. The respondent No.1 in his objection has denied the entire averments of the petition filed against him and denied that he is the owner of the offending Honda Motorcycle.
The respondent No.1 denied that involving him any accident took place on 30.09.2023 at about 22.45 hours on the alleged place of accident.
He denies that connected with the alleged accident a case is registered in the Kumbalagudu Police Station, in Crime No.313/2023.
He further denied that the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

On all other grounds,
prays to dismiss the petition.
6. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the medical and funeral expenses of the deceased.

Further admitted the issuance insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JV-9678 and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the rider of the offending vehicle.
Respondent also seeks protection under section 147 and 149(2) of M.V. Act.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the version of the petitioners remains unchallenged and undisputed.
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
14. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

15. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near ACS College, Kengeri Hobli,
Bengaluru South, when the rider of Honda motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-JV- 9678 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against to the deceased's motorcycle and caused the accident.

The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.

Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P6 was also filed as against the driver of the Eicher School Bus.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 and 5 coupled with Ex.P.11 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the rider of the Honda motorcycle.

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.
Even in the instant case the rider of the Honda motorcycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.

Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent riding of the Honda Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-JV-9678 by its rider.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.

and 3 :

It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
19.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was was studying B.Com and also working as a Swiggy delivery boy as part-time job and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not produced any document to show the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased, the court has to take into consideration the notional income.
Considering the work of the deceased and year of the accident is 2023, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month.
20 . It is stated that the deceased was aged 20 years at the time of the accident.
To prove the age of the deceased, PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of DL and Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P12 and Ex.P13 which shows the date of birth as 19.12.2003.
The accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 20 years.

As such, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '18'.
21.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 20 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

As such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m..
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents and he was a bachelor.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 50%(1/2) of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,200/-
p.m.(Rs. 22,400 - Rs.11,200 = Rs.11,200/-).
22. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,200/- p.m. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.24,19,200/- (Rs.11,200 X 12 X 18).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.24,19,200/- under the head of loss of dependency.
23. In this case, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the mother and father of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an Lakshmi Devamma M vs Darshan S D on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26956443/

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

24. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

27.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.2 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-JV-9678.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative and issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,40,200/- (Rupees Twenty Five lakhs forty thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 50% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 and 5 coupled with Ex.P.11 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the rider of the Honda motorcycle.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
17. Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent No.1 counsel at length, nothing is elicited from her mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P5 and Ex.P9 coupled with Ex.P11 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle rider.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
19.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was was studying B.Com and also working as a Swiggy delivery boy as part-time job and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not produced any document to show the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased, the court has to take into consideration the notional income.
The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents and he was a bachelor.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an Lakshmi Devamma M vs Darshan S D on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26956443/
7 accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 50% Petitioner No.2 - 50% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
